questions.q: Per the EASA FAQ, how long is an A1/A3 or A2 pilot certificate valid in the EU?
options: 2 years
5 years
10 years
indefinitely, if there are no violations
questions.explain: EASA: "A certificate for Remote Pilot competency is valid for 5 years". Renewal before expiry is a seminar with the authority or a recognized entity; after expiry, competency has to be demonstrated again; in Czechia renewal opens no earlier than 180 days before expiry.

questions.q: What does the EU A2 certificate require beyond the A1/A3 proof?
options: A class 2 medical and 10 hours of flying with an instructor at a recognized entity
Registration of a class C2 aircraft and operator insurance
An in-person flying exam at a recognized entity
Self-practical training under A3 conditions, a declaration of it, and an additional exam with the authority
questions.explain: UAS.OPEN.030: self-practical training under A3 conditions, a declaration of it, and an additional theoretical exam with the competent authority with a score of at least 75 %.

questions.q: How often must a Part 107 certificate holder complete FAA recurrent training to stay current?
options: every 24 calendar months
every 12 months, with a new test at a center
every 36 months, an FAA online course
only when changing aircraft
questions.explain: FAA: online recurrent training every 24 calendar months; the ALC-677 course is free. Only the initial test at a center is paid, about $175 per the FAA FAQ.

questions.q: The Czech online A1/A3 test at dron.caa.gov.cz: what format does the ÚCL page state?
options: 30 questions, 70 % to pass, 45 minutes
50 questions, 80 % to pass, 90 minutes
40 questions, 75 % to pass, 60 minutes
40 questions, 60 % to pass, no time limit
questions.explain: ÚCL: 40 questions with one correct answer out of four, 75 % to pass, a 60-minute limit; the minimum pilot age is 16.

questions.q: In the UK, what happens to the GVC (General VLOS Certificate) according to the CAA page?
options: It replaced the A2 CofC from January 1, 2026 and is needed for any paid work
It is issued until December 31, 2027; after that, RPC-L1/L2/L3 remain
It is needed for any flight heavier than 250 g
The CAA issues it directly after an online test
questions.explain: CAA: "The GVC will stop being issued on 31 December 2027"; after that, RPC-L1, L2, L3. GVCs already issued remain valid to the end of their term (5 years), if the authorization accepts them.

questions.q: The role is embedded engineer. Of 10 skills, 3 are fully covered, 4 partly, 3 not at all. What is the weighted coverage under the module's rule?
questions.explain: (3 + 0.5 × 4) / 10 = 50 %. 30 % is the strict coverage, 70 % counts partial skills as whole, and 47 % counts modules (8 of 17) instead of skills.

questions.q: What does the module require, at a minimum, of every portfolio piece?
options: A flight video and a social media post
Configurator screenshots, a customer review and a link to a channel with flights
A pilot certificate and a photo of the aircraft
A config, the original log, a README with the result in numbers, a video and FMEA rows
questions.explain: The course portfolio standard is reproducible artifacts: a config (diff all / .param), a log with a plot, a README with a number, a short video, an FMEA. The "Systems thinking" criterion requires the same.

questions.q: Per PX4's CONTRIBUTING.md, how are commit messages and PR titles formatted?
options: conventional commits: "type(scope): description", checked in CI
"Subsystem: description", under 72 characters
free text; what matters is the issue link and the author's Signed-off-by
the issue number and the author's name in square brackets
questions.explain: PX4 uses conventional commits, for example fix(mavlink): …; the PR title is checked by CI. The "Subsystem: description" format is ArduPilot's rule.

questions.q: What does the module say about salary figures for a "drone pilot"?
options: BLS gives a median for drone pilots for 2025
An EU average is published by Eurostat
There is no separate occupation in the BLS classification, so the module gives no pilot figures
Surveys by flight schools and blogs are reliable if they are under a year old and polled more than a hundred people
questions.explain: The module uses only official statistics with a year and a country: BLS, May 2025, aerospace engineers $134,960, technicians $82,890. BLS has no "drone pilot" occupation, so no pilot figures are given.
